title: A proof run is kept only outside the repository for the provider's attestation, and never committed
when: With a git repository: GitHubAttestations hands over a proof run with a predicate file outside the repository, and then with a predicate file in the repository.
then: The predicate names the commit and is outside the repository, with the digest the store returns. The repository has no change and no new commit. The second hand-over is refused and writes nothing.

title: The delivery object is written into the project folder, where version control keeps it
when: With the service of the test data set: stego apply runs.
then: Expects the ApplicationSet to be written under the project folder, at the path the plan names, and to be shown by git status as a new file to commit.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The outcome of the delivery check is kept as an attestation on the image, from either provider
when: With the test repository of the test data set: a push runs the generated pipeline to its end on the hosted CI provider; then a push of the service with the delivery stanza that names Konflux runs the generated PipelineRun to its end.
then: Expects each published image digest to have an attestation among its OCI referrers whose subject is that digest and whose predicate names each of the five STEGO checks with its result.
notes: Needs the hosted CI provider and its attestation store, and Konflux or the stand-in that ST-DLV-TD05 names. The Konflux run is the case that catches an attestation that only one provider's path writes.

title: STEGO keeps no delivery store of its own
when: With the service and the images of the test data sets, and HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME and the temporary folder each set to a new empty folder: stego apply runs, then stego delivery check runs on the hosted image.
then: Expects each of the five folders to be empty after the runs, and no file to change outside the project folder and those folders.
notes: Compare a listing of the whole test folder before and after the runs, so that a store in an unexpected place is caught.

title: A crash at any point of apply leaves the old record with the old files, or the new record with the new files after the next run
when: With an applied project in a temporary folder and a plan that creates, updates and deletes files: apply is stopped with SIGKILL at each journal point in turn, and after each stop the next run of stego recover runs.
then: Expects each stop before the journal is written to leave the old record and the old files. Expects each later stop, after recovery, to leave the new record and exactly the new files. Expects no stop to leave a record that does not match the files.
notes: It needs a test hook that stops apply at a named journal point.

title: Apply saves the record after every generated file
when: With an applied project in a temporary folder: apply runs a plan that writes three files, and the test records the order of the renames in the project folder.
then: Expects the rename of .stego/state.yaml to be the last write of the run.
notes: The test records the order through a file system wrapper or by tracing the system calls of the run.
